tools.name: get_context
tools.description: Returns the universal context-setting primer for Hemrock models, plus an optional template-specific addendum. Always run this first before any other prompts.

tools.name: get_prompts
tools.description: Returns task-specific Layer 2 prompts for a given template and task type. These are ready-to-use prompts for common modeling tasks.

tools.name: get_checks
tools.description: Returns Layer 3 sanity-check and validation prompts — the 'where AI gets financial modeling wrong' guidance. Use these to audit AI-generated work or catch common modeling errors.

tools.name: get_best_practices
tools.description: Returns Hemrock's financial modeling best practices and design principles for a given topic. Useful as background context for AI interactions.

tools.name: list_concepts
tools.description: Lists Hemrock financial-modeling concept docs — the methodology behind the math (exit waterfalls, anti-dilution, convertibles, cohorts, circular references, unit economics, and more). Returns a compact index of slugs, titles, and descriptions. Optionally filter by template_name or tag. Call get_conc

tools.name: get_concept
tools.description: Returns the full text of a single Hemrock concept doc by slug. Use this to learn how a financial-modeling calculation actually works before building or auditing it. Get valid slugs from list_concepts.

tools.name: list_models
tools.description: Lists the hosted Hemrock calculation engines (cap table, exit waterfall, fund economics, and the free unit economics, SaaS forecast and ecommerce forecast models), what each computes, and its price and checkout link. Free and needs no sign-in, so call it when the user asks what Hemrock can calculate

tools.name: get_access
tools.description: Returns public access terms for an engine: product, annual price, billing period, annual allowance, and a customer checkout URL. This is informational and does not purchase or confirm account-specific access; use get_account_access for the authenticated account.

tools.name: get_account_access
tools.description: Returns whether this connection is signed in, its annual product access and remaining calculations. Does not consume allowance. tools.description: Returns signed-in usage history and endpoint/source breakdown. Does not consume allowance. If the result contains action_required (not signed in, no purchase, allowance used), relay it to the user with its links and offer to retry. Never skip the calculation silently.

findings.detail: Description of "fund_economics_compute" is 4005 chars, far longer than this server's median (423). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_access, fund_economics_compute, list_saved_models, create_saved_model, request_review · Private data: fund_economics_compute · Public sink: cap_table_compute, fund_economics_compute, unit_economics_compute, saas_forecast_compute, ecommerce_forecast_compute, update_saved_model · Destructive: get_context, get_account_access, fund_economics_compute, run_saved_model, update_saved_model.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_access, fund_economics_compute, list_saved_models, create_saved_model, request_review · Private data: fund_economics_compute · Public sink: cap_table_compute, fund_economics_compute, unit_economics_compute, saas_forecast_compute, ecommerce_forecast_compute, update_saved_model · Destructive: get_context, get_account_access, fund_economics_compute, run_saved_model, update_saved_model

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
